- AFFO (adjusted funds from operations, the REIT earnings measure) was $1.15 per share, up 4.9%. That is slower than the roughly 7% growth earlier in the year.
- 2026 AFFO guidance went to $4.58–4.59, from $4.57–4.59.
- Investment guidance was cut to about $1.6B, from $1.6–1.8B.
- Dispositions (property sales) guidance was raised to $100–150M. About $200M of sales are expected from Q4 into Q1 at sub-6% cap rates.

- **Cap rates.** Acquisition cap rates were 7.3% in Q3, up 30 basis points from Q2. Management expects about 25 more basis points of expansion in Q4. The CEO said there is "no rush to deploy at yesteryear's pricing."
- **2027.** Management targets mid-single-digit AFFO growth per share. It assumes no further cap-rate expansion or yield-curve change.

I found no company-specific catalyst for today's +4.8%. The stock looks like a broad bounce from an oversold level. I found no coverage dated Nov 20 for either Indian IT or Wall Street, so the explanation for today's move is an inference.

**The story**
- **Q2 FY27 results (Oct 23):** Constant-currency revenue grew 1.5% year on year. Operating margin was 21.0%, and large-deal contract value was $5.2B, 62% of it net new, including one deal over $2B.
- **Guidance cut:** FY27 revenue growth guidance went to 1–2% from 1.5–3%. Margin guidance stayed at 20–22%. Analysts had expected the top end to fall only to 2.5%.

- **Pressure:** The CFO cited pricing pressure, competition and clients demanding a share of AI productivity gains. Nomura said the guidance cut came from lower price increases and softer volume. Revenue fell in manufacturing, retail and hi-tech.

- **Share reaction:** The ADR fell 6.6% to $12.35 on Oct 23 on about 46M shares.

  - The Q2 filing discloses that Infosys is "in discussions" with the US Department of Justice over how it classified certain H-1B visa holders. Infosys says it can't predict the outcome or whether it would be material.
  - The same disclosure appeared in earlier filings, so reports differ on how new it is. The Indian share price fell about 2.5% on Oct 27 on the news.
  - On Oct 7, Infosys was one of eight firms suspended from the US permanent labor certification program. Management says this has no effect on attrition or costs.
  - Infosys paid $34M in 2013 to settle an earlier visa probe.
- **Analysts:** Post-Q2 targets range from Rs 902 (Nirmal Bang, Sell) to Rs 1,425 (Asit C Mehta). CLSA moved to Hold at Rs 1,003. PL Capital is at Accumulate with Rs 1,200, and Emkay is at Buy with Rs 1,300. One aggregator shows the consensus as Hold.

**MTZ: what the story is and what could move it (12:15 PM CT, Fri 2026-11-20)**

I couldn't find any source that explains today's 12.6% drop, so the cause is partly inferred. The likely trigger is a new $1.25B acquisition announced today, which would explain the selling.

**How the stock got here**
- Shares peaked at $441.43 on May 6, 2026. They are down about 57% in six months.
- On Oct 29–30, Q3 2026 results beat on the headline numbers.
  - Revenue was $5.15B, up 30%.
  - Adjusted EPS was $2.96.
  - Backlog was a record $24.5B.
- Under that, guidance and quality were weak.
  - 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $18.3B, but adjusted EBITDA guidance came down to $1.565–1.600B and adjusted EPS to $8.92–9.30.
  - Implied Q4 adjusted EPS is about $2.35–2.73, below Q3.
- Pipeline Infrastructure had a 10.4% EBITDA margin, down 500 bps. Permitting delays started awarded projects about 60 days late and left crews idle. Work not finished in 2026 slips into 2027.
- Communications revenue fell 11.8% and its margin was 6.7%, down 460 bps. Customers deferred spending, citing a possible fourth wireless carrier and reorganizations at major customers.
- Power Delivery (+65%) and Clean Energy are carrying the growth. Part of Power Delivery's growth comes from the Superior Group acquisition, an electrical contractor bought in July.
- Net debt is $3.69B, up from $1.93B at year-end 2025, after the Superior deal.
- Four analysts lowered targets after the report: Cantor to $270, TD Cowen to $310, Truist to $332 and Jefferies to $353. All four kept Buy ratings. The 52-week low touched $147.32 today.

**Capital allocation (my read)**
- Nov 5: MasTec suspended late-stage talks on a large acquisition to prioritize its $250M buyback. That is about 2% of the roughly $13B market cap. The release says talks could resume.
- Nov 20 (today): MasTec announced a definitive agreement to buy Murphy Corporation, a mechanical contractor for mission-critical and data center work.
  - The cash price is about $1.25B plus a three-year earnout. A bank term loan funds it.
  - Murphy is projected at about $775M revenue and $140M adjusted EBITDA in 2026. That is roughly 9x EBITDA.
  - MasTec says net leverage is 2.7x as of Sept 30 and will fall below 2.0x during 2027. Closing conditions are substantially met.
- The deal reverses the Nov 5 message about buybacks, adds leverage while the base business is soft, and follows a guidance cut. I think that is the most plausible reason for today's drop.
- Only one aggregator page (Stock Titan) lists the Murphy deal. I did not open the press release itself, and no page showed a price reaction.

**What could move the stock over the next 1–10 sessions**
- **Down:**
  - Further market stress. Investing.com's sidebar showed the S&P 500 and Dow in correction and the VIX at 32. I couldn't confirm that figure from the market sources.
  - Forced or tax-loss selling in a name down about 21% in five sessions.
  - Analyst cuts that treat the deal as too much leverage.
- **Up:**
  - A bounce from oversold levels.
  - Buyback news or an investor-call defense of the deal.
  - Analyst support for the data-center strategy, which is the bullish framing.
  - Insider buying. I found no November 2026 Form 4 purchases, and the 2026 insider activity I found was director sales near $300–417.
  - A market rebound.
